fatal_blockers: Proposal 1 is algebraically dead as stated. With the changed port’s diagonal block still I4, its energy for fixed other ports is ||b||^2+ell^T b+const; the existing hybrids satisfy h+h'=b0+b1 and ||h||^2+||h'||^2=||b0||^2+||b1||^2, so their energy-sum identity survives arbitrary cross-port blocks uP,vP,wP. Escaping requires a nonseparable within-port self-Gram or additional charged joint coordinates, not merely cross-port coupling.

Proposal 2 has no bounded experiment: “rational centers” have no finite parameterization, and enumerating cuts for a fixed graph does not by itself synthesize emitted port maps or prove the required inequalities. The min-cut theorem may certify a fully specified first-kind lattice, but the proposed search does not specify one complete NAND/COPY CVP construction.

Proposal 3 is the only repairable survivor, but its stated test is unsound: excluding the four false Boolean fibers still permits Delaunay vertices with malformed non-Boolean port images at exactly legal energy. Every one of the 27 shell vertices must map to a legal truth-table word, and the empty-sphere certificate must be emitted explicitly.

Proposal 4 does not specify how nonlinear constant-weight membership, normalization, affine target offsets, and unrestricted malformed residue ports are emitted linearly. Finite coset-leader tables alone do not establish complete gluing or depth-two transfer, and zero-syndrome states require explicit accounting rather than the false assertion that they automatically pay positive leader norm.

Proposal 5’s charged carries destroy the claimed periodic finite residue closure: shifting a port and compensating its carry changes epsilon||k||^2. Its rational offsets and epsilon values are also unbounded, while setting epsilon=0 restores G1/G7.

Proposal 6 cannot use all 240 E8 roots as an empty legal shell. Antipodality forces any common center to be orthogonal to every root and hence zero, while the lattice point zero lies strictly inside the root sphere.

Proposal 7’s bounded rank-6 enumeration cannot prove the proposed universal no-go theorem. Toric circuits among legal columns neither quantify over every lattice point nor automatically produce one adverse integral point on or inside the sphere.

No proposal currently supplies COPY, complete unrestricted transfer closure, or lambda/mu>=65/64. Even a successful local shell experiment remains finite frontier evidence and cannot be promoted to recursive growth or hardness.
evidence: The supplied Generation-5 verifier establishes only that the separable K tensor I4 family fails through a hybrid energy identity; it explicitly leaves genuinely different Voronoi codebooks open. No verifier evidence is supplied for any current proposal.
The stronger identity above directly refutes Proposal 1 without enumeration because its proposed perturbations alter only terms linear in the recombined port.
